reason: the design fails 2 of its checks

findings.text:
DSFSTG-1: 1 part to fix
DSFSTG-1[code]: --from-stage <s> rehydrates all stages before <s> and dispatches <s> as the first stage covers: RQFROM-1 RQFROM-2
  Given: A previous run completed stages before <s>; their artifacts are present in the git state branch; a new invocation uses --from-stage <s>
  When: The runner starts with --from-stage <s>
  Then: The artifacts from every stage before <s> appear in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR before the dispatch loop starts
  And: Stage <s> is dispatched as the first unit — when <s> is a cycle stage, a cycle.start event is emitted for <s> and stage.start is emitted for <s>'s first cycle member; when <s> is a leaf stage, a stage.start event is emitted for <s>; no corresponding dispatch event fires for any stage before <s>
  And: No stage.start event is emitted for any stage before <s>
  And: `pipeline.skip_to_stage` is emitted when `--from-stage` is active; no stage before <s> is dispatched after that event [FIX IN DESIGN: The fourth And — "pipeline.skip_to_stage is emitted when --from-stage is active; no stage before <s> is dispatched after that event" — asserts that the event IS emitted as a positive obligation, but RQFROM-2's words impose no such obligation: they prohibit only the sequence (emit then earlier-stage dispatch). The positive assertion "is emitted" adds a requirement the issue does not state. — say what someone could see happen, not how it is built]

DSITER-1: 1 part to fix
DSITER-1[code]: Cycle orchestrator reads current_iter from persisted state on resume and starts the iteration loop from that value; fresh runs and nested-loop re-entries always start at iter=1 covers: RQLOOP-1
  Given: A run is being resumed; persisted state records cycle_iterations[CYCLE_ID].current_iter=2 (iter 1 completed before interruption); _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true is exported
  When: The cycle orchestrator's run body executes
  Then: The iteration loop starts at iter 2, not iter 1
  And: No stage.start event is emitted for any iter-1 stage
  And: When _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE is false or unset (fresh run or nested-loop re-entry), the loop starts at iter=1 [FIX IN DESIGN: The third And — "When _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE is false or unset (fresh run or nested-loop re-entry), the loop starts at iter=1" — identifies the flag by name rather than observing an output: "iter=1" is a loop-counter value internal to the cycle orchestrator's run body, not an output, result, file, or event a test can read after the When. The observable proxy would be an event emitted for the first iteration's members. — say what someone could see happen, not how it is built]

answers: design finding 1: done — Changed DSFSTG-4 from [done] to [code]. The design checker's finding is correct: the branch moved the guard after the auto-resume check, so the working copy code is wrong for the `status=in_progress` scenario. Specifically, the branch's pre-auto-resume check at the flat-path only catches `interrupted` status (not `in_progress`), so for a state file with `status=in_progress`, auto-resume fires and sets `resume_mode=true` before the post-auto-resume guard, allowing `--from-stage` without `--resume` to proceed. The DSFSTG-4[code] SPEC uses exactly this scenario (flat-path state file with `status=in_progress`): test FAILS on branch code before Gap 12 fix (auto-resume fires first) and PASSES after (guard restored before auto-resume). Added Given/When/Then accordingly, added the `[#1805/DSFSTG-4]` sub-case to the from-stage-rehydrate-test.sh step, added DSFSTG-4 to TESTFILES, and updated Findings 1, 3, and 32.

acceptance-gate finding 1: wrong — The DSFSTG-4[code] test is specifically the `status=in_progress` scenario where the branch's regression is observable. In the branch code (before Gap 12 fix): auto-resume fires for `in_progress` state via the flat-path check at line 2241, sets `resume_mode=true`, and the post-auto-resume guard at line 2320 doesn't fire → no error, test FAILS. After the fix (guard moved before auto-resume): error raised, test PASSES. The base code satisfies RQFROM-4 universally (guard at line 1737 fires before `state_file` is even set), so the same test passes on base code. For this regression-fix SPEC, the test fails on the working copy before the fix and passes after — the base code having the right behavior does not invalidate the [code] classification required by the design checker, since the working copy regressed it.

lens-correctness-design finding 1: wrong — The design already addresses this. Gap 11 documents the problem: after `skip_until_stage` is cleared when the target unit is found (in both dispatch-unit arms of `main()` in runner.sh), `resume_mode` is immediately also set to `false`. This prevents the resume skip guard (`$resume_mode && [[ -z "$skip_until_stage" ]]`) from activating for all subsequent leaf stages. DSFSTG-3[code] pins the observable behavior (stages after `<s>` that are marked complete are still dispatched, no stage.skip emitted). Finding 31 and the Decision paragraph both document this explicitly. The fix is `[[ -n "$skip_until_stage" ]] && { skip_until_stage=""; resume_mode=false; }` in both arms.
